logp.method_description: The log P value was determined by using the “shake flask” method. Octanol was used as the organic phase, and water was employed as the aqueous phase. The analyzed complex was solubilized in 150 μL of dimethyl sulfoxide, partitioned into three tubes containing 50 μL of the solvent each. Then, 975 μL of n-octanol and 975 μL of water were added, which was followed by stirring at 1000 rpm and 296 K for 24 h. The phases were separated, and the concentration of the complex in the organic phase was determined by UV-Vis spectroscopy, by using a calibration curve previously prepared for the complex, in dimethyl sulfoxide. The log P value was calculated by applying eqn (1): log P = log(Co/Ca) where Co and Ca are the molar concentrations of the complex in the organic and aqueous phase, respectively; Ca can be obtained by subtracting the initial concentration of the complex in the organic phase from Co.
